column2: Trim the ends and side strings of the beans; wash and cut into 3–4 cm pieces.
Slice the onion into half-moons; peel and dice the tomatoes.
Heat the olive oil in the pan and soften the onion for 3–4 minutes.
Add the beans and stir for 5 minutes; when their colour brightens, add the tomatoes.
Add the hot water and salt; cook covered over low heat for 35–40 minutes until the beans are tender.
Remove from the heat and leave to cool with the lid on; olive-oil dishes taste best warm or at room temperature.
Slice the courgettes into half-moons and dice the onion; grate the tomatoes.
Wash the rice until the water runs clear and drain.
Add the courgettes, rice and water; cook covered over low heat for 25 minutes until the courgettes and rice are soft.
Peel the aubergines in stripes and cut them; soak in salted water for 15 minutes to remove bitterness, then squeeze and pat dry.
Chop the onion finely and dice the tomatoes.
Add the mince and cook for 7–8 minutes until its liquid has evaporated and it has changed colour completely.
Add the tomatoes and aubergines and stir for 3 minutes; add the water.
Cook covered over low heat for 25 minutes until the aubergines are soft.
Pre-steam the cauliflower for 8 minutes until slightly soft.
Whisk the yoghurt, egg and olive oil and toss with the cauliflower; spread in the dish.
Scatter the cheese on top and bake for 20 minutes until the egg is fully set and the top is golden.
Remove from the oven and rest for 5 minutes; it will be easier to slice.
Wash the spinach 2–3 times in plenty of water to remove all grit; drain and chop roughly.
Add the spinach a handful at a time and let it wilt; add the rice and water.
Cook covered over low heat for 20 minutes until the rice is soft.
You can serve with garlic yoghurt.
Trim the okra stems into a cone shape without opening the pods; wash and drain.
Toss the okra with the lemon juice and leave for 10 minutes; this reduces sliminess.
Add the okra and water; cook covered for 25–30 minutes without stirring, gently shaking the pan instead.
Cut off the roots and tough green tops of the leeks; slit them lengthwise and rinse the soil from between the layers with plenty of water.
Slice the leeks into 2 cm rings and the carrots into half-moons.
Heat the olive oil in the pan and sauté the carrots for 3 minutes.
Add the leeks and stir for 5 minutes until they shrink.
Add the rice and water and cook covered over low heat for 25–30 minutes.
Squeeze over the lemon and stir; serve warm.
Keep the artichoke bottoms in lemon water so they don't discolour.
Heat the olive oil in the pan and sauté the onion and carrot for 4 minutes.
Add the peas and stir for 2 minutes; arrange the artichokes cup side up.
Mix the lemon juice with the water and pour in; cook covered over low heat for 25–30 minutes until the artichokes are tender.
Add the carrot and stir for 3 minutes; add the potato and peas.
Add the hot water; when it boils, lower the heat.
Cook covered for 25–30 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Preheat the oven to 200°C; line a tray with baking paper.
Peel the vegetables and slice them evenly; keep the beetroot separate so it doesn't stain the others.
Toss the vegetables with the olive oil and thyme.
Arrange on the tray in a single layer without touching.
Bake for 30–40 minutes.
Turn the vegetables with a spatula halfway through so every side browns evenly.
Test with a fork: if it slides in easily, the vegetable is cooked.
Grate the courgettes and leave with a pinch of salt for 5 minutes; then squeeze out the liquid firmly with your hands.
Mix the courgette, egg, flour and dill; the batter should be thick enough not to run off the spoon.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat with a little oil; spoon in small portions of the mixture and flatten.
Cook each side for 3–4 minutes until fully cooked inside and golden underneath.
Drain on kitchen paper to remove excess oil; serve with yoghurt.
Break the cauliflower into florets, wash and dry thoroughly; if it stays wet it won't brown.
Toss with the oil, ground red pepper and a little salt.
Spread on the tray in a single layer.
Bake for 25–30 minutes.
Slice the leeks and chop the carrot.
Add the leek and sauté for 5 minutes; add the rice and water.
Cook covered over low heat for about 30 minutes until tender.
Slice the courgettes thinly, about 0.5 cm thick.
Arrange the courgettes in the dish, slightly overlapping.
Melt the butter in a small pan and cook the flour for 1–2 minutes; add the cold milk gradually, whisking until smooth and thick.
Pour the sauce over the courgettes and scatter the cheese.
Bake for 30 minutes until the courgettes are tender and the top is golden.
Peel the aubergines in stripes and prick them in several places with a fork; bake on a tray for 20 minutes until soft.
Slice the onions thinly, chop the garlic finely and dice the tomatoes.
Soften the onion in half the olive oil in a pan for 6–7 minutes; add the garlic and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomato and cook for 5 minutes; season with salt.
Slit the aubergines lengthwise, open the insides with a spoon and fill with the mixture.
Lower the oven to 180°C; drizzle with the remaining oil, add half a glass of water and bake for 25 minutes.
Cut the ends off the courgettes and hollow them out with a corer without piercing the skin.
Knead together the rice, mince, finely chopped onion, grated tomato, tomato paste and a little salt.
Fill the courgettes loosely to three-quarters, since the rice will swell.
Stand the stuffed vegetables upright and tightly in the pan so they don't fall apart; place an upturned plate on top.
Add hot water to come halfway up; when it boils, lower the heat and cook for 35–40 minutes.
Cut one open to check: the rice should be soft and the mince fully cooked.
Serve hot with yoghurt.
Chop the dill and crumble the cheese.
Mix the courgette, egg, flour, dill and cheese.
Spread 2 cm thick on a tray lined with baking paper.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until golden on top.
Insert a toothpick in the centre: it is ready if it comes out dry and the egg is fully cooked.
Break the cauliflower into florets and boil in salted water for 8 minutes; drain.
Spread the cauliflower in the dish and pour the sauce over it.
Scatter the cheese and bake for 20 minutes until golden.
Dice the carrot and potato small.
Arrange the artichokes in the pan cup side up; fill them with the carrot, potato and peas.
Add the olive oil, the juice of the remaining lemon, a little salt and 1 glass of water.
Cover with baking paper and the lid and cook over low heat for 30–35 minutes until the artichokes are tender.
Halve the courgettes lengthwise and scoop out the insides with a spoon, leaving 0.5 cm at the edges.
Chop the onion finely and dice the tomato.
Add the tomato and the scooped-out courgette flesh and cook for 4 minutes.
Divide the filling among the courgettes and arrange on the tray; add half a glass of water to the bottom.
Bake for 25 minutes; scatter the cheese and bake for 8–10 more minutes until the courgettes are tender and the cheese golden.
Scrub and wash the potatoes well; cut into wedges, peeled or unpeeled.
Soak the potatoes in cold water for 10 minutes to remove starch; dry thoroughly.
Toss with the oil, thyme, paprika and a little salt.
Arrange on the tray in a single layer.
Bake for 35–40 minutes.
Slice the courgettes evenly 1 cm thick; pat dry with kitchen paper.
Toss with the oil, dried mint, red pepper and a little salt.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until the edges are golden and the insides soft.
You can serve with yoghurt.
Slice the leeks into rings and dice the potatoes and carrot.
Heat the olive oil in the pan and stir the carrot for 3 minutes.
Add the leek and potato and sauté for 5 minutes.
Add the hot water; cook covered over low heat for 25 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Preheat the oven to 190°C; line a tray with baking paper.
Wipe the mushrooms with a damp cloth; don't soak them. Remove the stalks and chop finely.
Place the mushroom caps upside down on the tray, bake for 8 minutes and pour off the liquid.
Turn the caps over and fill with the chopped stalks, a little oil, thyme and cheese.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until the mushrooms are soft and the cheese has melted and browned.
Peel the celeriac, carrot and potato and cut into even pieces; keep the celeriac in lemon water so it doesn't discolour.
Place the celeriac in the pan first, with the carrot and potato on top.
Add the olive oil, orange juice, a little salt and enough water to come halfway up the vegetables.
When it boils, cook covered over low heat for 30–35 minutes until the celeriac is tender.
Break the cauliflower into florets and boil in salted water for 6–8 minutes until slightly soft; drain.
Scatter the cheese and bake for 20 minutes until golden on top.
Peel and dice the celeriac, carrot and potato; keep the celeriac in lemon water so it doesn't discolour.
Heat the olive oil in the pan and stir the vegetables for 4 minutes.
Add the orange juice, water and a little salt.
Cook covered over low heat for 30 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Wipe the mushrooms with a damp cloth and slice; don't soak them.
Slice the onion thinly and chop the pepper finely.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and soften the onion and pepper for 4 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and sauté over high heat for 6–8 minutes until their liquid has evaporated.
Add the thyme and salt and stir for 1 minute.
Grate the courgette and carrot; leave with a pinch of salt for 5 minutes and squeeze out the liquid firmly.
Chop the dill.
Mix the vegetables with the egg, flour, dill and oil.
Spread 2 cm thick in a small dish lined with baking paper.
